transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Two taps. That's me. If you're hearing this, I missed a check-in, and you're sitting in my chair because nobody else wanted the paperwork.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: He missed three. He told me once: one check-in is weather, two is trouble, three is worry. I've been worried since Tuesday.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Sparrow. You fly the pattern too low and too fast, and I never fixed it, because it's the only thing you do without asking permission.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Command calls it desertion. They made me say the word on the net. I said it. I'm not saying it again.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: If I miss your checkout, fly the pattern anyway. The sky will still be there.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: Three bandits on the rim and an empty chair. Fine. I'll fly the pattern.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The bandits wore our markings. Our paint, our numbers. One of them was a tail I cleared for departure in March.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The quartermaster found a case under Teal's bunk. A coffee tin, twelve tapes, and a note: 'For Sera. Not for the net.'

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Keep these off the command net. Somebody up there is listening and signing things they shouldn't. If I go quiet, the case goes to Sera. Only Sera.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: There's a manifest in the tin. Aviation fuel, shipped as grain, to five quays on Iron Coast. Nobody ships grain in drums.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Iron Coast is a hundred miles of our own shoreline. Whoever this is, they're not invading. They're already home.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: Then I'll go and look at the quays myself.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: I came home through the western switchback. Not the pretty way. The way you take when you don't want to be seen coming home.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: I dropped beacons on the way in. Low power, my own frequency. If anyone ever follows me, I wanted it to be someone who knew the song.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Recovery wanted to walk the canyon for him. Command said no: there are scouts in the rocks, and recovery teams don't carry missiles.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: He used to tune that canyon on Sundays. Said it was the only place the tower couldn't talk to him.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Recovery can reach his receiver if you mark it and stay on their frequency. Finding him is work we can do together.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: Then that's where he went when he had something to say.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Recovery got into the lower switchback. They found his receiver in the rocks. Cracked case, memory intact. He put it where it would be found.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: There's a radar inside our own training box. Dug into the bowl north of the pass. Nobody signed for it. I checked the ledger three times.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Somebody wanted to watch trainees. Not the sky. Trainees. Think about why you'd want to know when the kids fly.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: If it's real, it's been watching every pattern you've flown for a year. Command wants it gone quietly. I want it photographed first.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The staff list has to reach Varda after the strike. An erased radar can still leave a record nobody can explain away.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: If I just blow it up, it's a rumour. If I look at it first, it's a crime.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: The Teklan farmers let me hide a tape in a seed tin. The old woman asked my name, not my rank. Nobody at Varda has asked my name in ten years.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The radar's memory names that orchard. Three days later somebody ordered it evacuated. Now there are patrols firing on the evacuation trucks.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: They're not shooting at farmers. They're shooting at a seed tin. That's how badly someone wants Teal's tape back.

transcript.speaker: RUSK
transcript.text: ...three officers at Varda are being reassigned tonight. Their names are already off the roster. Nobody will ask. Nobody ever asks.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Count the trucks again at the road. I want names for the beds at Varda, not a report that says most of them got out.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: Those trucks are carrying somebody who asked his name. They get out.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The convoy made it. The old woman's granddaughter drove the lead truck. She marked three silos on the map with her thumb. 'Those smell wrong.'

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Three tanks under grain permits. Aviation fuel. The farmers know the difference, they just can't prove it. A fuel ledger would prove it.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Sparrow. Every unmarked silo in that valley is somebody's winter. Don't be the one who makes them hungry to make a point.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: He wrote that one for you. He never wrote anything for me. I'm choosing not to be hurt by that today.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The farm crew can read the ledger over your radio once the patrol is gone. Fuel burns. The names on the page must survive it.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: Three thumbprints. Three fires. Nothing else.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: One courier flies the frequency book through the dust pass every evening. Same time, same whine in the engine. Somebody should fix that bearing.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: We pulled his escort code out of the silo radios. Five fighters hide in the dust front with him. They'd rather lose him than drop what he carries.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: If the book is real, every relay on the plateau is in it. Every forged voice. Every name.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Scan the clearings before you chase. Then read me the packet on a clean channel; I want its words before command can rewrite them.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: Then I'd like to read it.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Not a frequency book. Tomorrow's orders. Varda tower 'compromised', the challenge code changed, my crew 'relieved' at 0400.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: If they ever call our tower compromised, check who changed the challenge code. The tower doesn't go bad. The code does.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: They've moved it up. They know we have the packet. Two flights are inbound and my crew is in the tower with a soldering iron and the old code on a napkin.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: I'm staying in the tower. In case you were wondering. I'm not leaving my chair for them.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Spotters are using the apron smoke. Mark the dishes first, and stay until our own flights answer the restored tower code.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: Keep the lights on, Sera. I'll keep the sky.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: The tower is ours again. The old code went out at 0353 and three flights turned around on hearing it. One didn't.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Vulture Lead followed me into the pass. He wasn't chasing a deserter. You don't chase deserters at night with your lights off. He was erasing a witness.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: He talks on the guard channel when he's hunting. Likes you to know. Don't answer him. Let the canyon answer.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: He's searching the night approach for you now. Same lights off. Same voice. He thinks he's finishing a job.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: He carries a recorder. Mark where it falls. Recovery should come home with more than another empty aircraft.

transcript.speaker: TRAINEE
transcript.text: He's starting one.

transcript.speaker: SERA
transcript.text: Vulture Lead is down. His recorder survived. He carried relayed 'emergency orders', dozens, every one signed by a governor who's been dead since spring.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Kiro talks to Lira. Lira talks to Merel. Merel talks to the harbours. Break one link and listen to who screams.

transcript.speaker: TEAL
transcript.text: Kiro keeps an archive. Every forged order, filed, because forgers are vain. It's the only honest thing on the plateau.
